description:
ClipBoard Manager with history, selection and management. Needs LSPosed / Root
ClipVault is a deliberately small clipboard manager: one screen with a search
bar and your copied entries, and one settings screen. Nothing else.

Tap any past entry to put it back on the clipboard - it's marked as the
active entry, and selecting it never creates a duplicate or reorders your
history.

Capture works without any of the usual clipboard-reading permissions, using
one of two builds (chosen when the app is compiled, not a switch inside it):

* LSPosed build (default) - a module hook installed into system_server reads
  clipboard writes system-wide, before Android's background-read
  restrictions even apply.
* Root/priv-app build - installed via a Magisk/KernelSU module straight into
  /system/priv-app, so a background service can read clipboard changes the
  way Android's own privileged clipboard tools do. Flash the module, reboot
  once, done.

Settings are limited to what a clipboard history actually needs:

* Private mode, to pause saving entirely
* A configurable history limit (or no limit)
* Clear history

ClipVault makes no network requests, contains no analytics or ads, and
stores everything locally on the device.

Requires either an active LSPosed module or root access to capture
anything - see the project README for setup instructions.

This app is fully AI generated. It's great though 🤷‍♂️

There should be two versions up on F-Droid,
the lower one using Xposed 93 and the higher one libxposed 102.
If one doesn't work maybe the other does!

It works for me on my Android 15, it should work from A13 upwards,
but users have reported it not working on A16.
Use the issue tracker if encountering any problems!
